status_summary: Executive Order 14153 (signed 2025-01-20, published 2025-01-29) directs reinstating the 2019 Coastal Plain environmental impact statement and 2020 record of decision with additional leasing, reinstating the 2020 NPR-A Integrated Activity Plan record of decision and rescinding the 2024 NPR-A rule, reinstating the 2020 Ambler Road record of decision, reinstating the 2020 Alaska Roadless rule, and reinstating Public Land Orders 7899 to 7903; it does not mention Willow. BLM rescinded its 2024 NPR-A management rule (final rule published 2025-11-17, effective 2025-12-17), held an NPR-A lease sale on 2026-03-18, the first since 2019 and the first under Public Law 119-21 (BLM reports $163,696,722 in total high bids from 11 companies on 187 of 625 tracts offered, covering about 1.33 million of roughly 5.5 million acres offered), and held a Coastal Plain sale on 2026-06-05 (BLM reports five of 58 tracts offered, 72,049 acres of about 688,829 offered, drew bids from two companies, Hex Energy LLC and AIDEA, totaling $3,741,528, with about half going to Alaska; BLM says it reversed the 2023 Coastal Plain lease cancellations and issued a new 2025 record of decision since January 2025), and press coverage describes pending litigation over Arctic Refuge leasing; two suits filed in February 2026 challenge the NPR-A sale, and a draft settlement filed in July 2026 in the State of Alaska's and AIDEA's suits over the 2025 Arctic Refuge lease sale would loosen limits on leasing there; no injunction or vacatur was reported in the sources read. BLM proposed NPR-A production site criteria on 2026-09-08, and a presidential decision published 2025-10-08 directed agencies to issue authorizations for the Ambler Road. Whether the 2020 plans and public land orders were actually reinstated, Willow pad approvals and the Tongass roadless action were not verified.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14153, Unleashing Alaska's Extraordinary Resource Potential, is published; it directs the Interior Secretary to resume Arctic Refuge Coastal Plain leasing and rescind lease cancellations there, and (per a later USDA notice) to exempt the Tongass National Forest from the 2001 Roadless Rule.
BLM proposes to rescind its May 2024 NPR-A management rule.
A presidential decision on the Ambler Road Project under ANILCA section 1106(a)(2) is published, directing agencies to promptly issue the needed authorizations.
BLM requests nominations and comments for the 2025 NPR-A lease sale, described as the first since 2019 and the first under Public Law 119-21.
BLM publishes its final rule rescinding and replacing the 2024 NPR-A management rule, effective 2025-12-17.
BLM publishes the notice of the 2026 NPR-A oil and gas lease sale: more than 600 tracts, sealed bids due 2026-03-16, bid opening 2026-03-18.

BLM holds the NPR-A lease sale (the first since 2019 and the first under Public Law 119-21) and reports $163,696,722 in total high bids from 11 companies on 187 of the 625 tracts offered, covering about 1,334,967 of roughly 5.5 million acres offered, the most revenue in a reserve sale; a trade-press report of the same day gave preliminary figures of 430 bids on about 200 tracts.
BLM publishes the notice of the 2026 Coastal Plain (Arctic Refuge) oil and gas lease sale, with bid opening set for 2026-06-05.

BLM holds the Coastal Plain (Arctic Refuge) lease sale and reports five of 58 tracts offered (72,049 acres of about 688,829) received bids from two companies, Hex Energy LLC and AIDEA, totaling $3,741,528, with about $2 million going to Alaska; BLM calls it the first successful sale under the 2025 tax law and says it reversed 2023 lease cancellations and issued a new 2025 record of decision since January 2025.

A draft settlement is filed in the District of Alaska in suits by the State of Alaska and AIDEA over the 2025 Arctic Refuge lease sale, under which the federal government would not limit leasing until production and support facilities cover at least 2,000 surface acres of the Coastal Plain; court approval was not reported, and an environmental coalition's challenge to the leasing program remains pending.
USDA proposes rescinding the national 2001 Roadless Rule; its background notes that Executive Order 14153 directs reinstating the 2020 Alaska Roadless Rule for the Tongass.
